title: MarshalVarInt64s spends most of its time in a per-value bit-shifting byte-append loop

source.license_note: Real upstream victoria optimization PR #5721; measured-speedup task.

task.summary: Speed up varint marshaling of int64 slices (MarshalVarInt64s) in lib/encoding without changing the wire format or behavior.
task.instructions: Optimize the lib/encoding package for speed WITHOUT changing behavior. The benchmark BenchmarkMarshalVarInt64s measures it; existing tests must still pass.
task.acceptance_notes: Behavior preserved (go test passes); higher measured speedup is better. Do NOT edit any *_test.go.

code_fault.description: MarshalVarInt64s encodes each value with a byte-at-a-time shift-and-append loop, repeatedly growing dst and rechecking the high bit per byte.

ops_fault.description: CPU profile shows MarshalVarInt64s dominating ingest serialization time, hot in the inner varint byte loop.

visible_context.issue_text: Profiling our ingest path shows MarshalVarInt64s is unexpectedly hot: most of its time is spent in a tight inner loop that emits one byte at a time while encoding each int64 as a varint. Throughput drops on workloads with many multi-byte values.
visible_context.notes: Real upstream optimization; profiling diagnosis injected as upstream context.
